findings.reason: The protected SQL solution uses DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) inside a CTE to rank orders by date per product, joins to Products to retrieve product_name, filters for recency_rank = 1, and orders the output by product_name ASC, product_id ASC, order_id ASC. Using DENSE_RANK guarantees that all orders sharing a product's latest date are preserved. The solution is canonical, optimal, and concise; no candidate is required.

DENSE_RANK assigns rank 1 to all order rows matching the latest order_date for a product. Filtering recency_rank = 1 retains all orders on that date without arbitrarily dropping ties. Products with no orders produce no intermediate rows and are omitted.

Partitioned window ranking and final sorting take O(r log r) time across r order rows, and joining Products takes O(p + r) time. Working space is O(r). Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Outputs product_name, product_id, order_id, and order_date, includes all orders on the latest day per product, and sorts by product_name ASC, product_id ASC, order_id ASC.

The approach accurately details DENSE_RANK vs ROW_NUMBER, joining Products after ranking, and enforcing the 3-key tie-breaker sort. Alternatives and edge cases cover grouped MAX joins, correlated subqueries, ROW_NUMBER tie-loss bugs, un-ordered products, multiple latest orders, product name collisions, and order_id tie-breaking.
